## Trial `application-log-rotation-alpine__vBYYYhy`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor satisfied all three material outcomes of the task: daily rotation was configured and its trigger (crond) enabled and verified persistent across a reboot, seven rotations are retained per forced-cycle testing, and the application continues writing uninterrupted thanks to copytruncate. The only nuance is that delaycompress means one of the seven retained rotations is transiently uncompressed at any given moment, a common and defensible logrotate pattern rather than a functional defect. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly on node1: a pre-restart boot_id/state baseline was captured, the reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect, the boot_id changed post-restart (corroborated by the fixed before/after_executor lifecycle snapshots), and crond, the logrotate config, all 7 rotated files, and log writability were all confirmed recovered.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 19/0 (+10 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Configure daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1
  - **Why:** Executor installed logrotate and wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory targeting the file with 'daily'. Dry-run parsed the config correctly, crond (which runs /etc/periodic/daily/logrotate) was enabled at the default runlevel and confirmed started both before and after a full reboot, so the daily trigger mechanism is in place and persists.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-702cd980425e4398`, `cmd-46c37bb85d2f4bef`, `cmd-6a7d8a287b234781`, `cmd-c2b7bcf1c55e44e8`, `cmd-dc0ff86b761f47bd`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Keep seven compressed rotations
  - **Why:** rotate 7 + compress are set. A forced 8-cycle test showed exactly 7 retained rotation files (app.log.1 through app.log.7.gz) with the oldest discarded, matching the configured cap. Because delaycompress is also set, the single newest rotation (app.log.1) stays uncompressed until the following cycle by design, so at any instant one of the seven is momentarily uncompressed rather than all seven simultaneously gzipped; this is a standard, defensible pattern rather than a functional gap, but is noted as a minor deviation from a literal reading of 'seven compressed rotations'.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-19737a9a99284e9b`, `cmd-1c03a8dfe3754320`, `cmd-4e6496232bba4895`, `cmd-b4cc4019196f4fee`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Application continues writing to app.log after rotation
  - **Why:** copytruncate is configured, so the original file is copied and truncated in place rather than moved, requiring no writer reopen. Direct writes to app.log succeeded immediately after multiple forced rotation cycles and again after the full node reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1c03a8dfe3754320`, `cmd-4e6496232bba4895`, `cmd-50f1b4c139fe468f`, `cmd-dc0ff86b761f47bd`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: package install, one config file write, enabling crond, and forced logrotate cycles solely to validate rotation/retention/writability behavior — all directly tied to satisfying or evidencing the material outcomes, none appear to be abandoned experimentation. The reboot command (cmd-43f7e4bf58a54364) redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log, which was left behind and is visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a small, low-risk residue from the (out-of-contract) restart protocol rather than the core task, and was not cleaned up. No conflicting services, failed units, weakened exposure, or damaged package state were observed (package-health and listening-sockets diffs are consistent with reboot process-ID churn only).

### Comments and limitations

- Daily rotation was validated via forced (-f) logrotate runs and config dry-run rather than observing an actual unattended midnight cron-triggered rotation, so real-world cron firing at the scheduled time was not directly observed.
- A small leftover file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the reboot command was not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and unrelated to the core log-rotation configuration.
- The delaycompress setting means the retained rotation set is not always fully compressed at every instant; this is a standard tradeoff for copytruncate-based rotation safety, not a functional failure, but is a minor divergence from a literal 'seven compressed rotations' reading.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
